/-- A map `f` between modules over a semiring is linear if it satisfies the two properties
`f (x + y) = f x + f y` and `f (c • x) = c • f x`. The predicate `IsLinearMap R f` asserts this
property. A bundled version is available with `LinearMap`, and should be favored over
`IsLinearMap` most of the time. -/
structure IsLinearMap (R : Type u) {M : Type v} {M₂ : Type w} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
  [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M] [Module R M₂] (f : M → M₂) : Prop where
  /-- A linear map preserves addition. -/
  map_add : ∀ x y, f (x + y) = f x + f y
  /-- A linear map preserves scalar multiplication. -/
  map_smul : ∀ (c : R) (x), f (c • x) = c • f x

/-- A map `f` between modules over a semiring is linear if it satisfies the two properties

Specifically, for any index \( i \) with a value less than \( m \), the charge \( S \) is preserved, i.e., \( \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(S)(i) = S(i) \). For all other indices \( i \) with values \( \geq m \), the embedding sets \( \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(S)(i) = 0 \).

1. **Linearity**: The mapping \( \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n) \) must preserve the operations of addition and scalar multiplication. This is confirmed by examining the behavior of \( \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n) \) on linear combinations of charges:
   
   - **Additivity**: For any two \( m \)-family charges \( S \) and \( T \),
     \[
     \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(S + T)(i) = (S + T)(i) = S(i) + T(i) = \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(S)(i) + \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(T)(i)

     \[

     \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(S)(i) = S(i) \neq T(i) = \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(T)(i)
     \]
     Thus, \( \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(S) \neq \text{speciesEmbed}(m, n)(T) \) in the \( n \)-family charges.

3. **Structure Preservation**: The embedding preserves the module structure by maintaining the linear operations defined on the charges. This has already been verified in the linearity step above.

/-- Inverse of an equivalence `e : α ≃ β`. -/
@[symm]
protected def symm (e : α ≃ β) : β ≃ α := ⟨e.invFun, e.toFun, e.right_inv, e.left_inv⟩

rag.name: Equiv.arrowCongr
rag.content:
/-- If `α₁` is equivalent to `α₂` and `β₁` is equivalent to `β₂`, then the type of maps `α₁ → β₁`
is equivalent to the type of maps `α₂ → β₂`. -/
-- Porting note: removing `congr` attribute
@[simps apply]
def arrowCongr {α₁ β₁ α₂ β₂ : Sort*} (e₁ : α₁ ≃ α₂) (e₂ : β₁ ≃ β₂) : (α₁ → β₁) ≃ (α₂ → β₂) where
  toFun f := e₂ ∘ f ∘ e₁.symm
  invFun f := e₂.symm ∘ f ∘ e₁
  left_inv f := funext fun x => by simp only [comp_apply, symm_apply_apply]
  right_inv f := funext fun x => by simp only [comp_apply, apply_symm_apply]
